kernel_variant: Tier S2 tile_w4 + fp16 output. Same kernel body; final vstore4 down-casts to half and the output buffer is half-sized.
conclusion: fp16 output gave essentially zero speedup on the single-kernel benchmark (1.002 - 1.005x).
diagnosis: Output write of a 4K x 4K x 128 fp32 result is 8 MiB; at Adreno ~50 GB/s that's <200 us, less than 4% of the 5.7 ms kernel time. Halving the output to 4 MiB saves at most ~20 us per shape.
The actual bottleneck remains the inner-loop dot() / weight-read pipeline — output bandwidth was never on the critical path.

Value of fp16 output is therefore SYSTEM-LEVEL: it halves the downstream layer's input bandwidth, and is a prerequisite for fp32-buffer-less op fusion. It is not a perf win when measured in isolation.
Conclusion: keep the kernel as a building block for op-fused decode/prefill pipelines (§3.6), but stop expecting single-kernel speedup from this change alone.
